title: Field Coverage Time Calculator: Acres per Hour
description: Estimate how long fieldwork takes with the Field Coverage Time Calculator — from working width, speed and field size. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 60 ft boom at 5 mph covers approx. 36.4 acres per hour — so a 160-acre field is about 4.4 hours of pure travelling time.
quick_answer: The Field Coverage Time Calculator estimates how long a field operation takes from implement width, speed and the field's area. It converts width × speed into acres (or hectares) per hour and divides your field by it — the planning figure behind spray days, drilling windows and contractor quotes.
steps_intro: Width times speed is coverage; the field divided by coverage is time. Both halves matter:

body.t: A weather window is a number of hours. This calculator tells you whether the field fits inside it before the tank is filled — rows and passes from the
Per-hour and per-acre quotes both hide a coverage rate. Compute yours and the quote becomes a conversation about efficiency, not a mystery.
Choosing between two boom widths is choosing between two coverage rates. Run both against your largest field and the price difference gets a time value.
Combines, carts and trucks queue around one coverage rate. The estimate frames the whole chain's day.

60 ft boom × 5 mph: coverage = (60 × 5 × 5,280) ÷ 43,560 ≈ 36.36 acres/hour. A 160-acre field: 160 ÷ 36.36 ≈ 4.4 hours of travelling — plus fills, turns and the trip there, which the FAQ is honest about.
A 24 m boom at 8 km/h covers 24 × 8 ÷ 10 = 19.2 ha/hour; a 50 ha field takes ≈ 2.6 hours of travelling. The metric formula (width × speed ÷ 10) is the same idea in tidier units.

popular_table.title: Coverage rates at a glance
popular_table.intro: Theoretical field capacity: width × speed (imperial ÷ 43,560 after converting), before efficiency losses — real work runs at 60–85% of these figures.
popular_table.note: Theoretical capacity assumes non-stop travelling. Field efficiency (turns, fills, overlaps) is the real-world discount — experienced operators apply their own percentage.

faq: Time for a field operation: theoretical coverage rate from working width and speed, divided into the field's area, in hours.
Yes — instant and account-free, like the rest of the site.
The travelling-time core is exact arithmetic. Real jobs add turning, filling, overlap and travel between fields — treat the answer as the floor and add your operation's known overheads.
The share of engine time actually covering ground. Headland turns and refill stops eat the rest; 65–85% is the range textbooks quote for spraying and drilling, and your own records beat any table.
Does implement width mean the boom or the bout width?
The effective covered width per pass — usually the boom or bout width minus any overlap you drive. Overlap is pure loss in this formula, as it is in the field.
Width in metres × speed in km/h ÷ 10 gives hectares per hour — the formula used in the second example.
Can it price a contractor job?
It frames the hours; the rate per hour is the market's. Hours × rate is the quote's skeleton, whoever builds it.
Two fields, one day — how do I plan?
Compute each field's travelling time, add the road move between them and your fill/setup overheads. The day plan is a sum, and this tool supplies its biggest terms.
Not in the travelling figure — that is exactly what field efficiency discounts. Wide headlands and short fields lower efficiency; long lands raise it.
